answer.rationale: Compliance forbids reverting the security patch, so rollback is unavailable despite the release timing. Circuit breaking would drop customer writes and violates the objective. Failover is not supported by a described regional fault and risks write loss during peak settlement cutover. Read-replica routing matches report/read offload, not the stated heavy write path. memory_b3 is the closest lesson: extra headroom kept write queues stable under surge. Adding capacity is the one move that can relieve write p99 without discarding writes. Uncertainty remains—b3 was pre-peak provisioning, not a mid-incident add, and a pathological patch may not yield to more nodes—so keep this a standard, not maximal, rollout.
